reviewFlags.1-r4: The title combines a vector proof with Euclid VI.31, which is the similar-figures theorem, not a vector proof. Split into separate routes before treating the two as one approach.
reviewFlags.2-r4: The rational-root theorem argument is a short algebraic divisibility proof closely related to parity/lowest-terms; it is not a wholly independent strategy.
reviewFlags.3-r4: The zeta Euler-product proof is valid but overlaps route 3-r2; treat it as a refinement/variant unless a distinct source-backed analytic argument is supplied.
reviewFlags.4-r1: Scope restricted to primes 1 mod m (with cyclotomic/order hypotheses); the construction does not establish arbitrary reduced residue classes.
reviewFlags.4-r2: The cyclotomic norm sketch is an outline; the order of a modulo a prime divisor and exceptional divisors must be justified for each stated progression.
reviewFlags.4-r3: This is a scope warning, not a proof. Preserve as a caveat/route note, not as a proof approach.
reviewFlags.8-r1: Smoothing is a distinct optimization proof, but the compactness/maximizer and pair-equalization iteration need to be made explicit in a full proof.
reviewFlags.9-r4: Hölder route as written proves only the finite-dimensional scalar-product case; it does not directly establish Hilbert-space Cauchy–Schwarz.
reviewFlags.10-r1: The shortest-path phrasing is geometric intuition, but asserting the Euclidean segment is shortest already encodes the triangle inequality; it is not foundationally independent.
reviewFlags.10-r3: Convexity of the Euclidean unit ball is equivalent to the triangle inequality under discussion; this route is dependent unless convexity is established independently.
reviewFlags.11-r1: The altitude/projection proof is a valid coordinate geometry derivation, but its route depends on perpendicular projections and Pythagoras.
reviewFlags.12-r1: This is a cosine-law/altitude derivation. It overlaps substantially with 12-r2; keep the trigonometric route distinct only if the source-backed steps differ.
reviewFlags.12-r3: Gram determinant expansion gives a linear-algebraic formulation of the same cosine-law factorization; it is related rather than wholly independent.
reviewFlags.13-r2: This is the Bézout proof of Euclid’s lemma and substantially duplicates 13-r1; rewrite the catalog route titles to avoid counting variants as distinct.
reviewFlags.15-r2: Lagrange’s theorem packages the same finite-residue permutation fact used in 15-r1; the proof dependencies should be shown.
reviewFlags.17-r3: Continued fractions use the same strictly decreasing Euclidean remainder recurrence as 17-r1; it is a reformulation, not an independent termination proof.
reviewFlags.18-r3: The lattice/subgroup argument is the ideal proof in additive-group language and overlaps 18-r2.
reviewFlags.19-r3: The idempotent construction and the ring-isomorphism construction are two views of the same CRT mechanism; flag this dependence.
reviewFlags.21-r2: Lowest-terms divisibility and prime-exponent parity are closely related UFD arguments; do not count as independent without a source/history justification.
reviewFlags.21-r3: The rational-root route is another divisibility formulation of the same reduced-fraction contradiction.
reviewFlags.22-r3: Euclid parametrization and coprime opposite-parity parametrization are essentially the same family; distinguish only the primitive-classification content.
reviewFlags.23-r1: The primitive-triangle lattice-index lemma needs its proof stated; triangulation alone does not imply each primitive lattice triangle has area 1/2.
reviewFlags.23-r3: This repeats the primitive-lattice-triangle triangulation strategy of 23-r1; not a separate proof family as stated.
reviewFlags.24-r2: This triangle-removal induction is distinct from edge deletion but relies on a nontrivial removable-boundary-triangle lemma, which must be stated/proved.
reviewFlags.25-r3: The binary-sequence map needs the ternary 0/2 encoding (not ordinary binary expansions) to avoid expansion ambiguity.
reviewFlags.26-r2: Argument principle / Rouché is an outline; the winding count and zero-count hypotheses must be supplied in a full proof.
reviewFlags.27-r3: This is the Lebesgue/absolute-continuity version of FTC and has stronger/different hypotheses than the classical continuous version.
reviewFlags.30-r2: The finite-cover refinement is a construction of the same nested interval / total-boundedness mechanism as 30-r1.
reviewFlags.30-r3: This uses compactness-sequential compactness equivalence, so it depends on a theorem closely equivalent to the desired result.
reviewFlags.31-r3: Complete plus totally bounded implies compact is itself a metric-space compactness theorem; identify the equivalence being invoked.
reviewFlags.32-r2: This is the standard proof of MVT via Rolle and overlaps the extremum proof of Rolle in 32-r1.
reviewFlags.33-r3: Cauchy’s integral formula route applies to analytic/holomorphic functions, not all real Cⁿ functions covered by Taylor’s theorem.
reviewFlags.34-r2: The inverse-function linearization proves the nonzero-derivative special case; it does not alone establish general 0/0 or ∞/∞ forms.
reviewFlags.34-r3: Logarithmic differentiation is a reduction of indeterminate power forms to L’Hôpital/Cauchy-MVT and is not a fully independent route.
reviewFlags.36-r3: Cotangent partial fractions and the sine product are closely related analytic product expansions; flag as related to 36-r1.
reviewFlags.37-r2: The exponential addition law is one standard derivation of Euler’s formula; it overlaps the power-series route in 37-r1.
reviewFlags.37-r3: Rotation composition is equivalent to the geometric definition/derivation of Euler’s formula and depends on identifying complex multiplication with rotation.
reviewFlags.38-r2: The complex exponential law is equivalent to repeated angle addition; it is not independent of 38-r1 without separate foundations.
reviewFlags.38-r3: Rotation composition and roots-of-unity geometry are closely related to the exponential route; clarify whether this is a distinct proof or interpretation.
reviewFlags.39-r2: Orbit-sum elimination is another leading-term proof and overlaps 39-r1.
reviewFlags.39-r3: Invariant-ring formulation restates the same generator/reduction argument; not an independent proof as written.
reviewFlags.40-r1: Do not naively substitute A for the indeterminate in an arbitrary matrix-polynomial identity. The coefficient-comparison argument is required.
reviewFlags.40-r2: The cyclic-subspace argument needs a proof that the characteristic polynomial of each restriction divides the full characteristic polynomial.
reviewFlags.40-r3: Zero diagonal alone does not imply the matrix is zero; the generalized-eigenspace nilpotence step is essential.
reviewFlags.41-r3: The split-exact-sequence proof is the basis-complement argument in categorical language and overlaps 41-r1.
reviewFlags.42-r3: The Grassmannian/rank count is the same addition-map kernel argument as 42-r2.
reviewFlags.43-r2: An eigenvalue induction still needs existence of an eigenvalue (typically the fundamental theorem of algebra); the route depends on that premise.
reviewFlags.43-r3: Self-adjoint invariant-complement induction is closely related to the Rayleigh quotient proof 43-r1.
reviewFlags.44-r1: Maximum element order alone does not establish a cyclic direct summand. The splitting lemma is an essential missing step.
reviewFlags.44-r3: Module classification over Z is essentially the structure theorem/SNF argument of 44-r2, not a separate proof.
reviewFlags.45-r2: Class-equation induction is sketched but the full case split and use of Cauchy’s theorem for the center must be supplied.
reviewFlags.45-r3: The route name combines polynomial and permutation constructions; identify one precise construction before treating it as a single proof.
reviewFlags.46-r2: Class-equation proof needs the standard split: if p divides |Z(G)| use the abelian case; otherwise some proper centralizer has the full p-part.
reviewFlags.46-r3: This route invokes Sylow existence and the p-group case; it is dependent on Sylow and should not be counted as independent.
reviewFlags.47-r1: Area ratios prove Ceva when the cevians concur; the converse requires a separate argument (e.g. two cevians meet, then the product condition forces the third through the same point).
reviewFlags.47-r2: The sine-rule proof is another conversion of Ceva’s side ratios and is related to 47-r1; state the concurrency/converse hypotheses carefully.
reviewFlags.47-r3: The barycentric determinant criterion is the coordinate form of the same product condition, not a fully distinct geometric strategy.
reviewFlags.48-r1: Wilson’s theorem gives a modular square root of −1, not the integer sum of squares by itself; Gaussian-integer factorization supplies the key extra step.
reviewFlags.48-r2: This is nearly the same Gaussian-integer splitting proof as 48-r1, with Wilson’s theorem omitted in favor of the quadratic-residue criterion.
reviewFlags.48-r3: Minkowski’s theorem is a substantial imported result; explicitly state the disk area/determinant hypotheses.
reviewFlags.49-r1: Gauss-lemma parity and the lattice-point count are tightly connected; the route must specify how the sign count equals the rectangle count.
reviewFlags.49-r2: Eisenstein’s lattice-point proof is closely related to the Gauss-lemma lattice count in 49-r1.
reviewFlags.49-r3: The Gauss/Jacobi sum evaluation is only outlined; the nontrivial sum evaluation remains to be supplied.
reviewFlags.50-r3: Algebraic closure is not needed for factorization into irreducibles over F; the essential uniqueness mechanism is that F[x] is a PID/UFD, so this overlaps 50-r1/r2.
